newsitem.title: UK: Pizza Express higher on franchise report.
newsitem.headline: Pizza Express higher on franchise report.

text.p: Shares in Pizza Express Plc. gained over four percent on Monday on a newspaper report the restaurant chain is poised to buy back most of its remaining franchises in a move which is likely to boost profits.
Pizza Express shares set a record high of 467p in early trade but slipped back to 464p by 0730 GMT, up 17-1/2p on the day. The overall market was down 0.3 percent at the time.

The Sunday Times said the company was believed to have agreed a deal to buy in 32 of 37 remaining franchises. It said the move was expected to boost profits by four million stg for a full year and make Pizza Express an attractive takeover target.

"The shares got a good write-up in the Times. Most of the franchise story is well known but it drew people's attention in a dull market, especially talk of it being a takeover target," one marketmaker said.
Dealers said Pizza Express was also likely to benefit from the release last week of favourable figures, when the company said pretax earnings rose 54 percent in the year to July.

"The results were excellent and the franchise buy-in is a positive move and should help earnings. The problem is that the company only gets four percent of turnover from a franchise restaurant," said Kleinwort Benson analyst Paul Slattery.
Slattery said the franchise buy-in would enable Pizza Express to gain control of mature, established businesses.
"There's also evidence that company-managed restaurants perform far better than franchise outlets," he added.
Slattery said Kleinwort Benson would remain buyers of Pizza Express stock.
